questions.question: After how many new cache entries does Dapper garbage-collect its query cache, and which entries does it remove?
questions.reference: Every 1000 cache insertions (COLLECT_PER_ITEMS = 1000) Dapper runs CollectCacheGarbage, which removes entries whose hit count is <= 0 (COLLECT_HIT_COUNT_MIN), i.e. queries that were never reused.

questions.question: Besides clearing the query cache, what else happens when PurgeQueryCache is called?
questions.reference: It also purges the TypeDeserializerCache and raises the QueryCachePurged event.

questions.question: How can I find out how many queries Dapper currently has cached?
questions.reference: Call SqlMapper.GetCachedSQLCount(), which returns the number of entries in the query cache.

questions.question: When list expansion padding is enabled, what block size are IN-lists of up to 150 items padded to?
questions.reference: Lists of up to 150 items are padded up to a multiple of 10 (lists of 5 or fewer items are not padded at all).

questions.question: Which database connections does Dapper treat as supporting array parameters natively?
questions.reference: Connections whose type name is NpgsqlConnection (PostgreSQL) or ClickHouseConnection; FeatureSupport marks them as supporting arrays.

questions.question: How is a list parameter sent when the database supports arrays, instead of being expanded into many parameters?
questions.reference: If FeatureSupport says the connection supports arrays, PackListParameters adds a single parameter whose value is the whole list instead of expanding it into one parameter per element.

questions.question: If I don't pass a commandType, how does Dapper decide whether my SQL is plain text or a stored procedure name?
questions.reference: CommandDefinition.InferCommandType treats SQL containing whitespace, operators, comments, semicolons or reserved words (the WhitespaceOrReserved regex) as Text; a bare single name is treated as a StoredProcedure.

questions.question: Which single-word SQL commands are treated as text rather than stored procedure names?
questions.reference: vacuum, commit, rollback and revert are matched by the WhitespaceOrReserved pattern, so they run as text rather than as stored procedures.

questions.question: What syntax injects a member's value into the SQL as a literal instead of a parameter?

expected.contains: Dapper supports literal replacements for bool and numeric types.

questions.reference: A {=name} token such as {=Admin}; Dapper replaces it with the member's value as a literal instead of a parameter (supported for bool and numeric types).

questions.question: When an empty list is formatted as a SQL literal, what SQL does Dapper produce?
questions.reference: (select null where 1=0)

questions.question: What error is raised when the splitOn column for multi-mapping can't be found in the result set?
questions.reference: An ArgumentException (parameter splitOn) with the message "Multi-map error: splitOn column '...' was not found - please ensure your splitOn parameter is set and in the correct order".

questions.question: What is the default splitOn value for the multi-mapping Query overloads?

expected.contains: public static IEnumerable<TReturn> Query<TFirst, TSecond, TReturn>(this IDbConnection cnn, string sql, Func<TFirst, TSecond, TReturn> map

questions.reference: splitOn defaults to "Id".

questions.question: Which flags can a command carry to control buffering, pipelining and plan caching?
questions.reference: CommandFlags has None = 0, Buffered = 1, Pipelined = 2 and NoCache = 4 (bypass the query plan cache).

questions.question: What flags does a new CommandDefinition get by default?

expected.contains: CommandType? commandType = null, CommandFlags flags = CommandFlags.Buffered

questions.reference: CommandFlags.Buffered.

questions.question: If I don't pass a command timeout, where does Dapper get the timeout from?
questions.reference: If no timeout is passed, SetupCommand uses SqlMapper.Settings.CommandTimeout when it has a value; otherwise the provider's default is left in place.

questions.question: Which provider-specific command properties (for example Oracle's) does Dapper set automatically when it creates a command?
questions.reference: When the command type has them, Dapper sets BindByName = true, InitialLONGFetchSize = -1 and FetchSize (from Settings.FetchSize when it is >= 0), via a cached generated init method.

questions.question: Why are the SingleResult and SingleRow command behaviour optimisations disabled by default?
questions.reference: So that errors raised by the database after the SELECT are still detected properly; SingleResult/SingleRow can stop the reader before those errors surface.

questions.question: What does Dapper do if a provider throws because it rejects the SingleResult or SingleRow command behaviour?
questions.reference: If the exception message mentions SingleResult or SingleRow (and the settings are still at their defaults), Dapper turns both behaviours off globally and tries the command again without them.

questions.question: How do I make Dapper map snake_case columns like first_name to a FirstName property?

expected.contains: public static bool MatchNamesWithUnderscores { get; set; }

questions.reference: Set DefaultTypeMap.MatchNamesWithUnderscores = true so underscores are ignored when matching column names to members.

questions.question: When mapping a column to a field, what order of preference does the default type map use between exact, case-insensitive, backing-field and underscore matches?
questions.reference: Exact match over underscore match, exact case over wrong case, backing fields over regular fields, and match including underscores over match excluding them.

questions.question: How can I tell Dapper exactly which constructor to use when materializing my type?
questions.reference: Put the [ExplicitConstructor] attribute (ExplicitConstructorAttribute) on the constructor; DefaultTypeMap.FindExplicitConstructor picks it up.

questions.question: How do I map columns to properties using my own rule, for example a column-name attribute?

expected.contains: public CustomPropertyTypeMap(Type type, Func<Type, string, PropertyInfo> propertySelector)

questions.reference: Create a CustomPropertyTypeMap with a Func<Type, string, PropertyInfo> selector that returns the property for each column name, and register it with SqlMapper.SetTypeMap.

questions.question: What parameter size does DbString use for short strings when no Length is set?
questions.reference: 4000 (DbString.DefaultLength), used when Length is -1 and the value is at most 4000 characters.

questions.question: What happens if I set IsFixedLength on a DbString but don't give it a Length?

expected.contains: If specifying IsFixedLength,  a Length must also be specified

questions.reference: AddParameter throws an InvalidOperationException: "If specifying IsFixedLength, a Length must also be specified".

questions.question: How does DbString pick the DbType for the parameter it creates?
questions.reference: IsAnsi and IsFixedLength choose between AnsiStringFixedLength, AnsiString, StringFixedLength and String.

questions.question: How does DynamicParameters handle parameter names that start with @, : or ?
questions.reference: DynamicParameters.Clean strips a leading @, : or ? from the name, so '@id' and 'id' refer to the same parameter.

questions.question: Why would reading an output parameter fail with 'Attempting to cast a DBNull to a non nullable type'?

expected.contains: Attempting to cast a DBNull to a non nullable type!

questions.reference: Output/return parameters are only populated once the data stream completes (after enumerating an unbuffered Query, or after the GridReader from QueryMultiple is disposed), so reading them earlier sees DBNull.

questions.question: How can I bind an output parameter's value back onto a property of an object after the command runs?

expected.contains: public DynamicParameters Output<T>(T target, Expression<Func<T, object?>> expression

questions.reference: Use DynamicParameters.Output(target, x => x.Property, ...) to bind an output parameter to a property or field of the target object.

questions.question: What error do I get if I read results from QueryMultiple out of order or read one twice?

expected.contains: Query results must be consumed in the correct order

questions.reference: An InvalidOperationException: "Query results must be consumed in the correct order, and each result can only be consumed once".

questions.question: What do Dapper's async methods require of the connection object?

expected.contains: Async operations require use of a DbConnection or an already-open IDbConnection

questions.reference: They need a DbConnection, or an already-open IDbConnection whose CreateCommand returns a DbCommand; otherwise an InvalidOperationException is thrown.

questions.question: When executing a command many times with the Pipelined flag, how many commands can be in flight at once?
questions.reference: Up to 100 commands (MAX_PENDING = 100) can be pending at once.

questions.question: What happens if I pass an array of parameter objects to a method that runs a single query, like Query?

expected.contains: An enumerable sequence of parameters (arrays, lists, etc) is not allowed in this context

questions.reference: An InvalidOperationException: "An enumerable sequence of parameters (arrays, lists, etc) is not allowed in this context".

questions.question: Why does Dapper reject a ValueTuple as the parameter object?

expected.contains: ValueTuple should not be used for parameters

questions.reference: It throws NotSupportedException: a ValueTuple's language-level names are not available to use as parameter names, and it adds unnecessary boxing.

questions.question: When using pseudo-positional parameters like ?id?, how many times may each parameter appear in the SQL?

expected.contains: When passing parameters by position, each parameter can only be referenced once

questions.reference: Only once; referencing a pseudo-positional parameter more than once throws an InvalidOperationException.

questions.question: Does AsList copy the sequence if it is already a List<T>?

expected.contains: public static List<T> AsList<T>(this IEnumerable<T>? source) => source switch

questions.reference: No. If the source is already a List<T> it is returned as-is; otherwise it calls ToList() (and null returns null).

questions.question: Which DbType does Dapper use for byte[] parameters?
questions.reference: DbType.Binary.

questions.question: Which XML types have built-in type handlers?
questions.reference: XmlDocument, XDocument and XElement (XmlDocumentHandler, XDocumentHandler, XElementHandler), which set DbType.Xml on parameters.

questions.question: Which methods do I implement to write a custom type handler for my own type?
questions.reference: Subclass SqlMapper.TypeHandler<T> and implement SetValue(IDbDataParameter, T) and Parse(object), then register it with SqlMapper.AddTypeHandler.

questions.question: How do I pass a DataTable as a SQL Server table-valued parameter?

expected.contains: public static ICustomQueryParameter AsTableValuedParameter(this DataTable table, string? typeName = null)

questions.reference: Call dataTable.AsTableValuedParameter("TypeName") and pass the result as the parameter value.

questions.question: In Dapper.Rainbow, how does Insert return the id of the new row?
questions.reference: It runs "set nocount on insert ... select cast(scope_identity() as int)" and returns that value as int?.

questions.question: In Dapper.Rainbow, what table name is used if the guessed table name doesn't exist?
answer_keywords: typeof(T).Name|type name|type's name|name of the type|class name
questions.reference: It falls back to the type's name in square brackets, e.g. [Product].

questions.question: How do I stop a property from being included in Dapper.Rainbow inserts and updates?
questions.reference: Mark the property with [IgnoreProperty] (IgnorePropertyAttribute with Value true).

questions.question: How can I track which properties of an object changed so I only update those columns?
questions.reference: Start a snapshot with Snapshotter.Start(obj), change the object, then call snapshot.Diff() to get DynamicParameters for only the changed properties.

questions.question: With SqlBuilder, how are several Where calls combined, and how does OrWhere differ?
questions.reference: Where clauses are joined with AND after a single WHERE; OrWhere clauses are joined with OR.

questions.question: What placeholder syntax does a SqlBuilder template use to mark where clauses get inserted?
questions.reference: /**name**/ placeholders such as /**where**/, /**select**/ or /**orderby**/ in the template SQL.

questions.question: How can I check a DbException's provider-specific error number without referencing the provider assembly?

expected.contains: public static bool IsNumber(this DbException exception, int number)

questions.reference: Use the IsNumber(number) extension on DbException from Dapper.ProviderTools, which reads the provider's Number property via reflection.

questions.question: Which MySQL connection string option is needed to use user-defined SQL variables with Dapper?
questions.reference: Add "Allow User Variables=True" to the connection string.

questions.question: How do I stream rows from a huge query instead of loading them all into memory?

expected.contains: Dapper's default behavior is to execute your SQL and buffer the entire reader on return.

answer_keywords: buffered: false|buffered = false|buffered to false|buffered=false|buffered parameter
questions.reference: Pass buffered: false to Query so rows are streamed as you enumerate instead of buffered into a list.

questions.question: Why can building SQL strings on the fly without parameters cause memory problems in Dapper?

expected.contains: if you are generating SQL strings on the fly without using parameters

questions.reference: Dapper caches information about every query in a ConcurrentDictionary; SQL generated on the fly without parameters creates a new cache entry per string, which can use a lot of memory.

questions.question: How can I parse different rows of one result set into different concrete types?

expected.contains: This is where `IDataReader.GetRowParser` comes in handy.

questions.reference: Use IDataReader.GetRowParser<T>(concreteType) to create one parser per type, then pick a parser per row (for example from a discriminator column).
